newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Henry Walker sees sales/profit hike.
newsitem.headline: Henry Walker sees sales/profit hike.

text.p: Contract miner and engineering firm Henry Walker Group Ltd said on Tuesday that its 1996/97 revenues should be around A$500 million and the group was on track for 10 percent growth in earnings.
"Total gross revenue for the group overall should be in the order of A$500 million for the full year," managing director Richard Ryan said in a statement.
Henry Walker achieved a net profit of A$17.7 million in 1995/96 on total revenue of A$441 million.
Ryan said projected contracting revenue for the 1996/97 would be around A$400 million.
"This figure compares with A$314 million in (1995/96) and provides a solid foundation upon which the company's target of ten percent growth in revenue and earnings can be pursued," he said.
"The company's order book at December 31 provides the combination of a strong contracting revenue for 1997 with a sound long-term position," he said.
Henry Walker said earlier on Tuesday that it achieved a 14 percent rise in net profit for the six months to December 31 1996 to A$10.8 million, and a 29 percent rise in revenue to A$258.1 million.

Ryan said the revenue growth was almost entirely due to the substantial expansion of the company's contract mining and civil engineering operations, through a 63 percent rise in the value of its order book in the past 12 months.
